record.original_question: For the hard-core lattice-gas partition function Z(w) on graphs of maximum degree Delta, what is the largest complex domain containing w=0 such that Z(w) is zero-free for all such graphs? This should account for both the equal-fugacity case and the unequal-fugacity case (where one asks for domains D such that Z(w) != 0 whenever every vertex fugacity w_x belongs to D).

evidence.quote: Question 2.4 What is the largest complex domain containing w = 0 on which Z(w) is zero-free for all graphs of maximum degree Delta? [This question has two versions, depending on whether the w_x are assumed equal or unequal.]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph. The independence polynomial (hard-core lattice-gas partition function) of $G$ in the multivariate form is
$$Z_G(\mathbf{w}) \;=\; \sum_{I \in \mathcal{I}(G)} \prod_{x \in I} w_x,$$
where $\mathcal{I}(G)$ denotes the set of independent sets of $G$ (including the empty set, contributing $1$), and $\mathbf{w}=(w_x)_{x\in V}$ is a tuple of complex vertex fugacities. The univariate version is $Z_G(w)=Z_G(w,w,\dots,w)$.

Fix an integer $\Delta\ge 2$ and let $\mathcal{G}_\Delta$ be the class of all finite graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$.

(a) (Equal-fugacity case.) Determine the largest open connected domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}$ containing $0$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{G}_\Delta$ and every $w\in D$ one has $Z_G(w)\ne 0$.

(b) (Unequal-fugacity case.) Determine the largest open connected domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}$ containing $0$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{G}_\Delta$ and every choice of vertex fugacities with $w_x\in D$ for all $x\in V$ one has $Z_G(\mathbf{w})\ne 0$.

Describe these maximal zero-free domains explicitly (or characterize them) as functions of $\Delta$.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made but the exact maximal zero-free domain is not fully determined. Peters and Regts (2017/2019) confirmed Sokal's conjecture, proving the existence of an explicit complex neighborhood of the real interval $[0,(\Delta-1)^{\Delta-1}/(\Delta-2)^\Delta)$ on which the (multivariate) independence polynomial does not vanish for any graph of maximum degree $\Delta$, and the radius is optimal along the positive real axis (Shearer's bound). Further work by Bencs–Csikvári, by Buys and others has refined this neighborhood, and the limit of the zero locus for bounded-degree graphs has been studied (2111.06451). However, the maximal complex zero-free domain containing $0$ remains not exactly characterized; the problem is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: On a conjecture of Sokal concerning roots of the independence polynomial
status_evidence.snippet: Peters and Regts confirmed Sokal's conjecture that for every Δ≥3 there exists a complex neighborhood of [0,(Δ-1)^(Δ-1)/(Δ-2)^Δ) on which the independence polynomial is nonzero for all graphs of maximum degree Δ.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a zero-free complex neighborhood is established; tight bound on positive real axis.

status_evidence.title: On the location of roots of the independence polynomial of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Refines the neighborhood given by Peters–Regts on which the independence polynomial is zero-free.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to enlarge/refine the known zero-free region, indicating the maximal domain is not yet fully known.

status_evidence.title: The limit of the zero locus of the independence polynomial for bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the limit of zero loci for bounded degree graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the exact maximal zero-free domain remains an active area.
